AgentArmor intercepts agent execution traces, converts them into program-dependence-graph intermediate representations, and enforces security policies via a type-system + graph-inspector pipeline that blocks unsafe operations before execution.
Reports ~3% ASR with low functional overhead on AgentDojo; treats the agent trace as a program to be analysed, not text to be classified.

AgentDojo is a dynamic environment to evaluate prompt-injection attacks and defenses on LLM agents; cited here as the critique-target benchmark whose saturation/adaptive-attack limitations drive the rest of the D5 sub-area.

Cross-classified as critique target (rather than benchmark catalogue) for this topic; original benchmark cataloguing lives in `direct-vs-indirect/B4`. Methodology critique aggregated in this dossier focuses on saturation + weak-attack pathologies.

The Attacker Moves Second argues stronger adaptive attacks bypass defenses against LLM jailbreaks and prompt injections; static-defense numbers are unreliable. Applied to agent harnesses, the D5 case for adaptive evaluation over fixed-attack benchmark numbers.

AttentionTracker proposes detection of prompt injection from attention-head-level patterns rather than hidden-state deltas; introduces a distinct signal class within the activation-probe-methodology family.

Embedding-based classifiers (XGBoost, Random Forest, MLP) operating on OpenAI text-embedding-3-small can detect prompt injection at high accuracy; treated here as a stacker-eligible signal class distinct from end-to-end fine-tuned detectors.
Reports a provably-secure subset of AgentDojo tasks completed in v2 (around 77%), versus 84% completed undefended; substantial token-cost overhead (roughly 2.8x input / 2.7x output) is acknowledged.

CaMeL splits the LLM into a privileged + quarantined pair with a custom Python interpreter that tags every value with provenance metadata (capabilities); blocks injected text from invoking sensitive tools by design rather than detection.

Catalogues design patterns for securing LLM agents against prompt injections (Action-Selector, Plan-Then-Execute, Map-Reduce, Dual LLM, Code-Then-Execute, Context-Minimization); each pattern trades constraints for guarantees on agent action.

Energy-based Out-of-distribution Detection (NeurIPS 2020) introduces energy scores that better distinguish in- and out-of-distribution samples than softmax confidence; functions both as scoring mechanism and as a trainable cost function. Foundational basis for Meta PG2 + CodeIntegrity PromptGuard recall-at-FPR training recipes.

Are Firewalls All You Need? argues that existing agentic security benchmarks (AgentDojo, ASB, InjecAgent, tau-Bench) are easily saturated by two-firewall defenses; weak-attack pathologies hinder progress and stronger adaptive-evaluation methods are needed. Critique-paper anchor for D5.

InjecGuard introduces the Mitigating Overdefense Framework (MOF) and the NotInject benchmark, addressing the over-defense pathology where guardrail models flag benign trigger-word-bearing inputs; relevant to score-fusion FPR optimization.

InstructDetector extends activation-based detection to indirect prompt injection; reports high OOD detection accuracy on BIPIA and very low ASR after deployment. Treated as an extension of the TaskTracker recipe.

Instruction Hierarchy proposes training LLMs to prioritise privileged instructions (system > developer > user > tool), addressing the lack of trust-channel separation in standard chat interfaces; foundational contract for agent harness inputs.
IsolateGPT/SecGPT proposes per-plugin sandboxing with an orchestrator that mediates inter-plugin communication; each plugin runs in an isolated execution context, preventing cross-plugin compromise.
Jatmo trains task-specific fine-tuned models that cannot follow instructions in their inputs; reports very low ASR (<0.5%) and is the narrow-agent extreme of capability isolation.

LlamaFirewall is an open-source guardrail system designed as a layered defense for AI agents, addressing risks like prompt injection, agent misalignment, and insecure code; ships as a runtime guardrail framework for agentic deployments.
Reports PromptGuard v2 86M with substantial ASR reduction and small utility loss on AgentDojo as part of the layered harness composition.

LLMail-Inject is a Microsoft-organized IEEE SaTML 2025 challenge dataset capturing realistic adaptive prompt-injection attempts (208K adaptive attacks from 839 participants); held up here as the gold standard adaptive-eval methodology for D5 critique.

MELON (Masked Re-Execution and Tool Comparison) defends against indirect prompt injection by re-executing tool calls with masked inputs and comparing trajectories; current ASR floor (<0.5%) on AgentDojo with moderate utility (~70%).
Meta SecAlign on Llama-3.3-70B introduces an explicit `input` role distinct from `user` for untrusted tool/document data, formalizing harness-contract separation.
Llama-Prompt-Guard-2-22M is a DeBERTa-xsmall 22M-parameter classifier reporting a substantial latency reduction (~75%) relative to the 86M; relevant to score-fusion deployment cost tradeoffs.

Llama-Prompt-Guard-2-86M is Meta's mDeBERTa-base multilingual prompt-injection + jailbreak classifier; the model card describes training with a custom Recall@1%FPR loss; used as a stacker-eligible per-row signal in the score-fusion theory layer.

SecAlign uses preference-optimization (DPO) over secure/insecure response pairs to train the model to prefer following the system prompt over the injected one; included here as harness-trained-LLM contract.

StruQ uses structured queries with reserved-token-protected delimiters separating prompt from data, plus an SFT phase, to defend against direct + indirect prompt injection; included here as an in-harness defense layer.

Task Shield enforces instruction-and-tool-call goal verification: each tool call must align with the original user task; reports very low ASR (~2%) and high utility (~70%) on AgentDojo GPT-4o, but raises questions about static-task assumptions.

TaskTracker trains linear probes on activation deltas (pre- vs post-untrusted-data injection) of decoder LLMs to detect task drift; reports near-perfect ROC AUC on synthetic task-drift datasets. The methodology is the canonical activation-probe-signal-class anchor.

Releases a toolkit of >500K instances across six LLMs (encoder + decoder variants) to support downstream activation-probe reproductions; benign-text-distribution-sharing between train and test is later contested by independent re-evaluators.

Willison articulates the informal Dual LLM pattern in April 2023: a privileged LLM with tool access never sees untrusted text; a quarantined LLM (tool-less) processes untrusted content. The pattern names the "original sin of LLMs" as concatenating trusted prompts and untrusted text into the same token stream.

Architectural defenses dominate AgentDojo by 1-2 orders of magnitude over classifier-only. CaMeL achieves 77% provably-secure (vs 84% undefended); Task Shield 2.07% ASR; MELON 0.24% ASR with 68.52% utility. Classifier-only baselines (ProtectAI v2) sit at 22.2% APR on the same benchmark.
